title: ClaimWithdrawStableStaker reward assertion lower band (9.9 phUSD) is loose enough to mask a materially wrong emission rate
description: The verification asserts rewardCredited in [9.9e18, 10.1e18] (EXPECTED_DAILY_PHUSD ±1%). The realized reward is 9999999999999936000 — only 64000 wei (6.4e-15 of 10e18) short of the 10e18 ideal, because phusdPerSecond = floor(10e18/86400) loses 64000 wei/day. The actual flooring dust is ~9 orders of magnitude smaller than the 1e17 (1%) band. The wide band is therefore a smoke-only tolerance: it would still pass if the deploy-set rate were off by up to ~1% (e.g. a config typo setting 9.95e18/day or an off-by-one in the per-second conversion). For a script whose stated purpose is to VERIFY the 10-vs-5 phUSD/day config split, a ±1% band on the rate it is verifying is weaker than the data supports.
impact: Smoke check only — it confirms reward accrues at roughly the right magnitude, not that the rate is exactly the configured 10 phUSD/day. A future deploy-config drift within 1% would pass verification silently. No funds impact; this is a test-strength / spec-fidelity observation on a verification script.
severityRationale: A weak-post-condition observation on a verification script: the reward band [9.9e18, 10.1e18] is ~1% wide while the real flooring dust is ~9 orders of magnitude smaller (64000 wei), so a future ~1% rate-config drift could pass the band silently. This has no funds impact and, critically, is partially mitigated by the script itself — STEP 1 already exact-asserts phusdPerSecond == 10 ether / 86400, which is the actual config guard, so the loose band is redundant rather than the sole line of defense against rate drift. It is a test-strength / spec-fidelity nit on tooling, the weakest-impact of the four, and sits at the informational end of QA: no security or availability dimension, and the suggested tightening is a quality improvement, not a defect that breaks anything today.
evidence: verify-stable-staker/side-effects.json realizedValues: rewardCredited 9999999999999936000, perDayFloorLoss_wei 64000, asserted band [9.9e18,10.1e18]. STEP 1 already exact-asserts phusdPerSecond == 10 ether/86400, so the rate itself is checked there; the reward-band check adds little beyond 'time advanced'.
recommendation: Tighten the reward band toward the actual dust (e.g. assert rewardCredited within a few thousand wei of 86400*phusdPerSecond using the on-chain phusdPerSecond, not a hardcoded 10e18 ±1%). The STEP-1 exact rate assert is the real config guard; the band is redundant and overly loose.
